world_money_map.summary: The current regime is restrictive but selective rather than uniformly risk-off. The Fed and BOJ have tightened, yet recent live controls show that action signs alone are poor price predictors when the moves are already priced: future-path/guidance surprise, relative rates, energy inflation and intermediation capacity matter more. The Sep. 15 U.S. tax/Treasury-settlement window produced a large TGA rebuild and reserve drain without a broad repo dislocation, materially weakening the idea that reserves plus ON RRP below about 10% of GDP is itself a scarcity trigger. At the same time, large broad U.S. equity-fund redemptions coexist with technology/financial/discretionary sector inflows, Asian equity inflows, government/short-duration bond demand, precious-metals inflows and a BTC rebound. Capital allocation is therefore cross-sectional and opportunity-cost-sensitive rather than a simple risk-on/risk-off switch.
world_money_map.regime: RESTRICTIVE POLICY / SELECTIVE CAPITAL ALLOCATION / EXPECTATION-SENSITIVE PRICING
world_money_map.liquidity: US RESERVES DRAINED ON SEP. 15-16, BUT REPO MEDIAN/TAILS REMAINED ORDERLY; AGGREGATE LIQUIDITY IS A SENSITIVITY VARIABLE, NOT A SCARCITY TRIGGER
world_money_map.credit: NO VALIDATED BROAD CREDIT OR FUNDING CRISIS; GOVERNMENT/SHORT-DURATION DEMAND STRONGER THAN HIGH-YIELD DEMAND
world_money_map.policy: FED TIGHTER; BOJ TIGHTER; ECB/BOE ALSO RESTRICTIVE OR INFLATION-SENSITIVE; MARKET IMPACT DEPENDS ON EXPECTATION-ADJUSTED PATH

money_flows.title: Broad U.S. equity funds are losing capital while selected sectors still receive it
money_flows.direction: BROAD US EQUITY FUNDS -> SELECTIVE SECTORS / OTHER ASSET BUCKETS
money_flows.confidence: HIGH on observed flows; MODERATE on destination inference
money_flows.summary: Reuters reported $31.44B of U.S. equity-fund outflows for a fourth consecutive week. U.S. sector funds still received about $2.29B, with financials, consumer discretionary and technology among the leaders. A broader global-fund dataset reported $23.21B global equity outflow but $6.26B Asian equity inflow and $4.49B sector-fund inflow.
money_flows.invalidation: Broad U.S. equity flows reverse and the sector/region dispersion disappears over several reporting periods.

money_flows.title: Government and short-duration fixed income retains relative demand
money_flows.summary: Despite weak aggregate bond-fund inflows, Reuters reported stronger demand for government and short/intermediate Treasury funds while high-yield and some credit buckets saw redemptions. This is consistent with investors demanding yield with less credit/duration risk under restrictive policy.

money_flows.title: Precious-metals funds are receiving capital while energy funds are not
money_flows.direction: COMMODITY FUND CAPITAL -> GOLD / PRECIOUS METALS OVER ENERGY
money_flows.summary: Global commodity funds received about $1.17B in the latest weekly data, concentrated in gold/precious metals, while energy funds had about $148M of outflows. This is observed allocation evidence, not proof of a durable gold bull regime.

money_flows.title: BTC ETF demand reversed positive for one completed session, but the short cluster remains net negative
money_flows.direction: MARGINAL SPOT BTC ETF DEMAND IMPROVED; DURABILITY UNCONFIRMED
money_flows.confidence: HIGH on completed flow data; LOW-MODERATE on persistence
money_flows.summary: Farside records +$159.5M U.S. spot BTC ETF net flow on Sep. 17 after -$450.4M Sep. 15 and -$295.9M Sep. 16. The three completed sessions remain net negative and the positive day was concentrated in IBIT. ETH remained -$39.3M on Sep. 17. Sep. 18 flows were unfinalized at the information cutoff.
money_flows.source: Farside Investors BTC/ETH ETF flow tables accessed Sep. 18, 2026
money_flows.invalidation: Several completed sessions of broad positive BTC/ETH creations with improving spot relative strength and healthy leverage would invalidate the current WAIT characterization.

money_flows.title: Treasury cash rebuilt sharply without validated broad funding stress
money_flows.direction: PRIVATE/BANK CASH -> TREASURY; RESERVES DOWN, BUT NO GENERALIZED REPO DISLOCATION
money_flows.summary: Fed H.4.1 shows Sep. 16 Wednesday TGA at $991.708B, up $148.003B week/week, and reserve balances at $2.921537T, down $114.971B. Yet Sep. 15 SOFR median and 99th percentile and TGCR 99th percentile rose only about 2 bp. The cash-drain mechanism realized; the scarcity transmission did not bind broadly.
money_flows.source: Federal Reserve H.4.1 and New York Fed reference-rate data

opportunities.title: Broad macro one-factor trade
opportunities.thesis: The live controls reject simple rules such as 'rate hike equals currency up/risk down' or 'reserve drain equals funding stress'. Oil, long yields, relative policy paths, growth/inflation information and positioning are pulling in different directions. No broad cross-asset directional edge clears the evidence bar.
confirmations: Consistent cross-market repricing in rates, USD, credit and equity breadth
Persistent flow evidence rather than one-day price reaction
opportunities.invalidation: A new asymmetric regime emerges with independent flow and price confirmation.

opportunities.title: AI/technology physical-investment chain
opportunities.confidence: MODERATE structural; asset-level LOW until valuation/cash-flow work is complete
opportunities.thesis: Sector fund flows and prior evidence of strong AI-related capex/financing support a structural capital-allocation theme across semiconductors, data centers, networking, power/grid and cooling. The canonical system does not yet have a valuation-adjusted individual-asset BUY thesis.
opportunities.capital_source_destination: Corporate/hyperscaler capex, credit financing and sector allocations -> physical AI infrastructure/value chain.
opportunities.invalidation: Capex commitments fall materially, financing tightens, utilization/monetization disappoints, or valuations imply returns below alternatives.

opportunities.title: Tokenized-securities infrastructure
opportunities.thesis: The SEC's Sep. 17 temporary conditional innovation exemption lowers a real regulatory barrier for tokenized NMS stock venues. Potential value capture should be mapped at venue, custody, settlement, liquidity and infrastructure layers rather than assumed to accrue to generic crypto tokens.
opportunities.capital_source_destination: Potential future securities trading/settlement activity -> compliant tokenized-equity infrastructure.
opportunities.invalidation: Low issuer/venue adoption, weak liquidity, adverse final rulemaking, legal challenge or economics accruing mainly to incumbents without public-asset capture.

opportunities.title: BTC after Sep. 18 rebound
opportunities.thesis: BTC reclaimed about $80k-$81k as Sep. 17 ETF flow turned positive, but the preceding two-day outflow cluster remains larger, Sep. 18 ETF flow is unfinalized, ETH flows remain weaker, and high-quality derivatives/exchange-flow decomposition is incomplete. A short-covering component is plausible but not primary-source validated.
confirmations: Several completed positive ETF sessions with breadth
Venue-grade OI/funding/liquidations show non-excessive fresh leverage
opportunities.invalidation: Large ETF redemptions resume, price fails to hold the rebound, or leverage rises sharply without spot breadth.

risks.title: High rates and energy inflation can re-tighten financial conditions
risks.summary: The Fed has tightened, the dollar is strong and oil remains above $100 even after its reversal. A renewed energy spike or further rate-path repricing could raise long yields and required returns, pressuring duration-sensitive assets.
risks.invalidation: Oil scarcity pressure continues to ease and long yields/real yields decline without a growth shock.

risks.title: Yen intervention risk after BOJ hike failed to strengthen JPY
risks.summary: USD/JPY rose toward about 158 after the expected BOJ hike as guidance disappointed hawkish expectations. Japanese authorities signaled concern, making intervention risk more relevant. This makes chasing the post-BOJ USDJPY move unattractive despite supportive carry.
risks.invalidation: Authorities tolerate sustained weakness and relative-rate spreads continue widening without intervention rhetoric/action.

risks.title: Middle-East energy route risk remains fat-tailed
risks.confidence: HIGH that tail risk exists; LOW on direction
risks.summary: Crude benchmark prices have eased as effective supply improved, but pipeline damage, constrained routes and refined-product bottlenecks remain. Fresh attacks or loss of substitute routes could rapidly restore scarcity premiums.
risks.invalidation: Route traffic normalizes, damaged capacity returns, physical differentials and product cracks normalize, and inventories rebuild.

risks.title: BTC rebound can be mistaken for durable accumulation
risks.summary: One positive BTC ETF session after two large negative sessions is not enough to establish a new institutional accumulation regime. The move may contain short-covering or broader risk-beta components.
risks.invalidation: Multi-session broad ETF creations, healthier spot relative strength and venue-grade derivatives/exchange evidence confirm durable demand.

causal_chains.title: Treasury cash rebuild -> reserve drain, but stress requires binding intermediation
causal_chains.summary: Tax/settlement flows -> TGA rises -> bank reserves fall -> potential repo sensitivity; however, if dealer/MMF/private intermediation and Fed backstops have capacity -> median and tail repo rates remain orderly -> no generalized funding-stress transmission. Sep. 15-16 is a matched non-crisis control.

causal_chains.title: Expected central-bank hike -> price response driven by relative path surprise
causal_chains.summary: Pre-event market embeds a likely action -> central bank delivers expected move -> headline contains little marginal information -> vote/guidance/future relative path becomes the shock -> FX/rates reprice accordingly. BOJ Sep. 18 and FOMC Sep. 16 both support this model.

causal_chains.title: Energy disruption -> price depends on effective deliverable supply
causal_chains.summary: Infrastructure damage -> expected shortage -> crude scarcity premium rises; rerouting, inventories, grade compatibility, product substitution and diplomacy alter effective deliverable supply -> benchmark premium can reverse even while physical-system stress persists.

causal_chains.title: Broad equity redemptions can coexist with sector accumulation
causal_chains.summary: Macro/rate uncertainty -> broad funds lose capital -> allocators still direct capital to preferred sectors/regions with stronger expected return narratives -> index-level outflow does not imply uniform selling across all equities.

discoveries.title: Aggregate Fed liquidity is a sensitivity condition, not a scarcity trigger
discoveries.summary: A roughly $148B TGA rise and $115B reserve decline occurred through the Sep. 15-16 event window without a broad median or 99th-percentile repo dislocation. Require actual intermediation/facility evidence before inferring funding stress.

discoveries.title: Expectation-adjusted policy path is more informative than action sign
discoveries.summary: The widely expected BOJ hike was followed by yen depreciation, while the heavily priced FOMC hike also produced a muted/offset cross-asset reaction. The future relative path, guidance and vote composition appear more informative than raw hike/cut direction; historical event testing is still required.

discoveries.title: Effective deliverable commodity supply matters more than headline damaged capacity
discoveries.summary: Brent reversed for several sessions despite continuing infrastructure/geopolitical stress as Saudi rerouting, inventories and diplomacy improved effective supply. Grade/location/product constraints still matter and can create local scarcity while the benchmark falls.

discoveries.title: Cross-sectional fund flows can dominate simple risk-on/risk-off labels
discoveries.summary: Large broad U.S./global equity outflows coexist with sector and Asian equity inflows plus precious-metals demand. Test persistence and relative-return value before generalizing.

changes_since_previous: The Sep. 15 tax/Treasury-settlement test is no longer a future risk: the TGA/reserve drain realized, but broad repo pricing stayed orderly. The deterministic scarcity thesis is materially downgraded.
The Sep. 16 FOMC and Sep. 18 BOJ now provide two live controls supporting expectation-adjusted policy-path reasoning over action-sign heuristics.
Broad U.S. equity-fund redemptions are now explicitly separated from positive sector/Asian allocations; the regime is selective rather than simply risk-off.
BTC ETF demand turned positive on Sep. 17 and BTC rebounded above $80k, but the three completed Sep. 15-17 sessions remain net negative and ETH flows remain weaker; stance stays WAIT.
The crude causal model is upgraded from gross outage size to effective deliverability by route/location/grade/product after substitution and inventories.
unknowns: Direct primary Standing Repo Facility take-up for Sep. 15-17 remains unresolved in this research lane; calm repo distributions make generalized stress unlikely but facility usage must not be inferred.
Sep. 18 BTC/ETH ETF flows were not finalized at the information cutoff.
Venue-grade BTC open-interest, funding, liquidation, exchange-flow and options-gamma data sufficient to separate spot demand from short covering have not yet been validated.
The expectation-adjusted policy-surprise hypothesis has only a small live-event sample and needs a timestamp-safe historical study.
It is not yet known whether current sector/region fund-flow dispersion predicts persistent relative returns after controlling for rates, earnings and valuation.
Middle-East energy logistics and diplomacy can change abruptly, leaving large directional uncertainty despite the current crude reversal.
research_frontier: Highest priority: obtain primary/venue-grade BTC derivatives and exchange-flow evidence and test whether the Sep. 18 rebound is spot accumulation, short covering, fresh leverage or a mixture.
Build timestamp-safe FOMC/BOJ/ECB event study comparing pre-event action/path probabilities with realized action, guidance/vote surprise and 30m/1d/5d FX/rates/equity/gold responses.
Build historical tax/Treasury-settlement controls stratified by aggregate liquidity plus dealer/MMF/intermediation conditions, using repo median/tails and official-facility usage.
Extend energy matched controls to route/location/grade/product deliverability, inventories, freight/insurance and physical differentials.
Test whether broad-equity outflows plus sector-tech inflows predict relative strength after controlling for rates, earnings revisions and starting valuation.
Map real fee/cash-flow capture under the SEC tokenized-securities exemption across venues, custody, settlement, liquidity and blockchain infrastructure.
